newsitem.title: UK: Aston Villa seeks London Stock Exchange listing.
newsitem.headline: Aston Villa seeks London Stock Exchange listing.

text.p: British soccer club Aston Villa Plc said on Thursday it planned to float on the London Stock Exchange in spring this year, joining a growing list of quoted football clubs.

The Birmingham club said it would raise between 15 and 20 million stg in new money from a share placing and offer for subscription. The company would be valued at between 120 million stg and 140 million, including the new money.
Aston Villa said the funds would be used to improve its Villa Park stadium, additional commercial facilities and to provide working capital.

"The commercial side of football is moving with terrific speed and we must therefore ensure we have every opportunity to continue to compete with the best in Europe, both on and off the field," Aston Villa chairman Doug Ellis said in a statement.
"I believe it is in the best long-term interests of the club to gain a listing at this time. Our 8,000 shareholders will also benefit from a more liquid market," he added.
Aston Villa said profits before interest and transfers totalled 5.8 million stg last year.

In the 1995-96 financial year and season, the club invested a net 5.8 million stg on players, helping it win the Coca-Cola Cup, reach the semi-final of the FA Cup and finish fourth in the Premier League, Aston Villa said.
Villa said most of its senior players were under 26 and had long contracts. The team's manager, Brian Little, recently signed a new five-year contract.
The club said attendance averaged over 35,000 per game this season at its 39,400-seater stadium.
